issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution implementation define Stock.take(String) to return an int (using -1 to indicate failure), but the template's Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This return-type mismatch will confuse students and may cause compilation or logic errors when they follow the specification/UML or the solution examples (which expect an int).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by changing the signature of Stock.take(String) in the template to return an int and adopt the same semantics (e.g., return -1 on failure, otherwise return remaining quantity). Update any template usages or comments accordingly so students implement against the same API described in the problem statement.
